result.title: Frame: Form-Restricted Authoring with Model-Based Evaluation
result.summary: Many professional reports reuse the structure of prior editions while updating the content. We formalize this setting as form-restricted report generation: given a sample report and new grounding documents, generate a report that preserves the sample's form while accurately reflecting the new evidence. We introduce FRAME, a benchmark of 120 EDGAR- and arXiv-derived instances across Financial Quarterly, Financial Annual, Academic Simple, and Academic Complex categories, built with a temporal three-snapshot pipeline. We evaluate outputs with three human-validated metrics: structural similarity via semantic tree-edit distance, coverage via information unit recall, and faithfulness via claim-level grounding verification. Across five LLMs, open-source models nearly match proprietary models on structure but lag on coverage and faithfulness; all models perform better on financial than academic reports, and performance declines with longer outputs and more complex grounding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FRAME 基准，将「沿用样例报告结构、按新 grounding 文档更新内容」形式化为 form-restricted report generation，包含 120 个金融与学术实例，并用结构相似度、信息单元覆盖率和 claim 级 grounding 验证三项指标评测五个 LLM。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 claim 级忠实度验证与信息单元召回指标，可能可供核查 LVR 中答案是否真正使用 latent 中的视觉证据、以及任务必要细节与结构保留的评价设计；但该工作为纯文本长文档生成基准，与多模态内部状态无直接联系。
